item.text:
**5B.4 Verdict:** mixed, leaning no. In 2024 Vietnam under Nguyễn Phú Trọng did move some rules in a pro-business direction, especially on land, credit, and energy approvals, but the anti-graft campaign and bureaucratic churn also created legal uncertainty, delayed approvals, and deterred investment. I did not find evidence of a clean, consistently fair competitive regime.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes, partial | Vietnam: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Vietnam | IMF | 2024-09-27 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/09/27/vietnam-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-the-555679 | The IMF said revised land, housing, real estate business, and credit-institution laws should reduce legal uncertainty, improve transparency in real-estate transactions, and support banking resilience. That is direct evidence of rule-making that helps property rights and investment conditions. | 5B.4 |
| Yes, partial | Vietnam approves data, electricity laws, $67 billion rail plan | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-11-30 | https://theprint.in/world/vietnam-approves-data-electricity-laws-67-billion-rail-plan/2381416/ | Parliament passed an electricity law meant to remove hurdles for energy investment and speed direct power purchase agreements. The package was pro-investment overall, though the new data law also tightened data-transfer rules that tech groups said could raise operating costs. | 5B.4 |
| Yes, partial | Vietnam says administration reform will not impact project approvals | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-12-20 | https://theprint.in/world/vietnam-says-administration-reform-will-not-impact-project-approvals/2411706/ | The government said the sweeping bureaucratic overhaul was intended to reduce red tape and simplify investment procedures. That supports a fairer, more predictable business environment in intent, even though the announcement itself reflects investor concern about possible delays. | 5B.4 |
| No / mixed | Exclusive-Vietnam forfeits billions of dollars in foreign aid amid anti-graft freeze, document says | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-17 | https://theprint.in/world/exclusive-vietnam-forfeits-billions-of-dollars-in-foreign-aid-amid-anti-graft-freeze-document-says/2088974/ | Reuters reported that administrative paralysis tied to the anti-corruption campaign caused lost aid, delayed approvals, and major deadlock. This is strong evidence that the operating rules were not functioning fairly or predictably for investment and project delivery. | 5B.4 |
| No / mixed | Foreigners sell Vietnam securities amid political turbulence, data show | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-17 | https://theprint.in/world/foreigners-sell-vietnam-securities-amid-political-turbulence-data-show/2089403/ | Foreign investors cut holdings amid political upheaval, with Reuters citing delayed project approvals and worries about power supply. That points to a business climate that was still unstable and rule-bound in ways investors did not trust. | 5B.4 |
| No / mixed | Vietnam misses out on Intel, LG Chem investments due to lack of incentives, ministry document shows | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-07-05 | https://theprint.in/tech/vietnam-misses-out-on-intel-lg-chem-investments-due-to-lack-of-incentives-ministry-document-shows/2162549/ | Vietnam reportedly lost major investments because it lacked sufficient incentives and a workable renewable-energy regulatory regime. This is direct evidence against having fully fair, competitive, investment-friendly rules. | 5B.4 |
| No / mixed | Viet Nam’s Economy Poised for Gradual Recovery, World Bank Report Finds | World Bank | 2024-04-23 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/23/viet-nam-s-economy-poised-for-gradual-recovery-world-bank-report-finds | The World Bank said private domestic investment and innovative firms still faced regulatory barriers, weak early-stage finance, and a need for simpler startup and investment procedures. That is good evidence that fair rules for entrepreneurship and competition were still incomplete in 2024. | 5B.4 |

**Search gap**
- I found concrete evidence of sectoral reform, but not a full, clean regime-wide transformation.
- I did not find strong evidence that Trọng personally built a level playing field for competition across the whole economy.
- The main counterweight is that anti-graft politics and administrative churn kept undercutting predictability even where reforms existed.
